solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Brazilian ready to follow team of stars (8)

indicatorNotes.to follow: what follows comes after, so REAL is placed after SIDE

blocks.note: the real is Brazil's currency, and ready (money) is cash

annotation.surface: A Brazilian footballer is poised to join an all-star team.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brazilian' looks like a player, but with 'ready' it means Brazilian cash: 'ready' is slang for money, and Brazil's unit is the real.
annotation.definitionFit: Sidereal is the astronomers' adjective for things relating to the stars, as in sidereal time.

entries.clue: Severely affected hand nurse holds (7)

indicatorNotes.holds: what holds something has it inside, so SEN goes round MITT

blocks.note: mitt is slang for a hand

annotation.surface: A nurse holds a hand that has been badly hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: SEN, a State Enrolled Nurse, is an old British nursing grade and a crossword stock nurse.
annotation.definitionFit: To be smitten is to be struck hard, by illness or by love.

entries.clue: Remixed vocal edit for Life of Riley (5,4)

indicatorNotes.Remixed: a remix rearranges a recording, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A sound engineer remixes a vocal track for a song called Life of Riley.
annotation.walkthrough: The music-studio words are all mechanism; the answer is the Italian 'sweet life'.
annotation.definitionFit: La dolce vita, the sweet life, is a life of carefree ease, which is what living the life of Riley means.

entries.clue: Uneasy setter’s supporting others (7)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue the support sits underneath, so IVE comes below REST

blocks.note: the setter says I'VE for 'the setter has'

annotation.surface: A nervous setter props up everyone else.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter is 'I', so 'setter's' is I'VE, with the apostrophe standing for 'has'.
annotation.definitionFit: Restive means restless and fidgety, uneasy under restraint.

entries.clue: Foolish time to start to climb up tree (7)

indicatorNotes.start to: the start of 'climb' is its first letter, C
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue 'up' means written bottom to top, so TOC turns into COT

blocks.note: APR 1, April the first, is All Fools' Day; the 1 is read as I
TO plus C (the start of Climb), reversed to read upwards

annotation.surface: A silly moment to begin scrambling up a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foolish time' is a date, APR 1, whose digit becomes the letter I. 'Up' reverses only TO and C.
annotation.definitionFit: The apricot is a fruit tree as well as its fruit.

entries.clue: Pieces invoking the name of great character (6)

blocks.note: pieces and gats are both slang for guns

annotation.surface: Writings that call on the name of a famous figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great' belongs to the title: Jay Gatsby is the hero of Scott Fitzgerald's The Great Gatsby. 'Pieces' means guns, as in gangster slang.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary reference: the novel's title calls its hero great, so the character in The Great Gatsby is literally a 'great character'.

entries.clue: Recruit in growth area giving up employment for navy (9)

indicatorNotes.giving up: the word gives up USE, so those letters leave
indicatorNotes.for: 'for' means in exchange for, so RN takes USE's place

blocks.note: GREENHOUSE, where plants grow, with USE removed

annotation.surface: A new recruit in a garden centre swaps his job for the navy.
annotation.walkthrough: Use is employment, as in putting something to use, so GREENHOUSE swaps its USE for RN.
annotation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a raw newcomer, just as a recruit is.

entries.clue: Cut heads on fish (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so TOPS comes above IDE

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: Someone chops the heads off fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb but is a noun: topside is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter.
annotation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean joint of beef, a cut from the butcher.

entries.clue: In pubs, one cheers brewer (7)

indicatorNotes.In: 'In pubs' places what follows inside the pubs, so the one, I, goes into BARS

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks

annotation.surface: In the pub, a man raises a toast to the brewer of its beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brewer' suggests beer to go with pubs and cheers, but a barista brews coffee.
annotation.definitionFit: A barista makes coffee, and making coffee is brewing it.

entries.clue: Clearly show strong desire to break into retail somehow (10)

indicatorNotes.to break into: LUST breaks into the other letters, so it goes inside them
indicatorNotes.somehow: 'somehow' means in some way or other, so RETAIL's letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A shopper shows an overwhelming urge to get into the shops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retail' looks like the setting, shops, but it is only a set of letters to rearrange around the desire.
annotation.definitionFit: To illustrate is to make clear by example or picture, to show clearly.

entries.clue: Employee benefit for every last piece of work (4)

indicatorNotes.last piece of: the last piece of 'work' is its final letter, K

blocks.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'

annotation.surface: A worker is paid a bonus for every finished job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece of work' suggests a finished job, but only the last letter of 'work' is wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: A perk, short for perquisite, is a benefit given to an employee beyond pay.

entries.clue: Dissertation about unknown number that is somewhere in the UK (3,3,8)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so THESIS goes round the rest

annotation.surface: A dissertation about some unknown number of places somewhere in Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: The Six Counties is a name, mostly used by Irish nationalists, for Northern Ireland.
annotation.definitionFit: Northern Ireland is made up of six counties, and it is part of the UK.

entries.clue: At last obtain a garment I will wear, the ultimate in green (7)

indicatorNotes.At last: 'at last' takes the last letter of 'obtain', N

blocks.note: I kept as is; as the wearer it goes on before the garment

annotation.surface: A shopper finally gets a green top to wear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I will wear' puts I in front of the VEST it wears. 'Green' is inexperienced, not a colour, so its ultimate is the superlative.
annotation.definitionFit: Green means naive, so the ultimate in green is the most naive, the naivest.

entries.clue: Full of vitality, agent recruits a couple of hands (9)

indicatorNotes.recruits: to recruit is to take in, so SPY takes RIGHT and L inside

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent
the two hands, RIGHT spelt out and L for left

annotation.surface: A lively agent takes on a couple of farmhands.
annotation.walkthrough: The two hands are right and left, one written in full and one abbreviated.
annotation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and energetic, full of vitality.

entries.clue: Of course, warning was rejected as expected (7)

indicatorNotes.rejected: rejected means thrown back, so WAS is turned round

blocks.note: fore! is the golfer's warning shout on the course

annotation.surface: Naturally, a warning was ignored, just as everyone knew it would be.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally' but means on a golf course, where the warning is FORE.
annotation.definitionFit: To foresee is to see ahead, so foresaw means expected.

entries.clue: National Theatre’s welcoming days stopped developing (9)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: a host welcoming a guest takes it in, so STAGE goes round NAT

blocks.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a whole

annotation.surface: The National Theatre, taking in some new days, has stalled.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Theatre's' is 'has': the theatre has NAT inside it, then D follows.
annotation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop moving or growing, so stagnated is stopped developing.

entries.clue: Fine stonework in church choir finally covered by board (7)

indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' takes the last letter of choir, R
indicatorNotes.covered by: what is covered is inside, so TRAY goes round CE and R

blocks.note: a tray is a flat board for carrying

annotation.surface: Delicate stone carving in a church, the choir stalls covered with boards.
annotation.walkthrough: The church-building picture fits the answer: tracery is the stone lacework in Gothic windows.
annotation.definitionFit: Tracery is ornamental stone openwork, especially in the upper part of church windows.

entries.clue: Having more showers is way to control foul air rising (7)

indicatorNotes.foul: foul air is spoilt, so its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the whole is turned round

blocks.note: a rein is a means of controlling a horse

annotation.surface: A wetter place needs a way to deal with foul air coming up.
annotation.walkthrough: REIN and the rearranged AIR make REINIAR, which then reads upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Rainier is the comparative of rainy, so it describes a place having more showers.

entries.clue: Roughly struck in the head, rebel falls (7)

indicatorNotes.in the head: the head of 'struck' is its first letter, S

blocks.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

annotation.surface: A rebel, roughly hit on the head, collapses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like the rebel's verb but is the noun, as in waterfalls. Jack Cade was an English rebel leader of 1450.
annotation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, and falls is another name for one.

entries.clue: Trick’s missed in unreliable moment (7)

indicatorNotes.missed in: the trick is missing from inside the word, so CON is removed

blocks.note: the start of INCONSTANT, before the CON
CON, the trick taken out of INCONSTANT
the rest of INCONSTANT, after the CON

annotation.surface: A trick fails at a shaky moment.
annotation.walkthrough: A con is a trick, and the unreliable word is INCONSTANT; taking CON from its middle leaves IN and STANT to close up.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an instant and a moment are both a very short space of time, as in 'wait a moment'.

entries.clue: Conclude not a single blazing thing! (7)

blocks.note: no means not a single one

annotation.surface: An investigator concludes nothing at all is on fire.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the surprise: the investigator's 'nothing is burning' spells out the very thing that is.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose description rather than a synonym: an inferno is a huge fire, and a fire is a thing that blazes.

entries.clue: Help someone easily deceived by reporter (7)

indicatorNotes.by reporter: a reporter tells the story out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a sucker is a gullible person
homophone indicator: SUCKER as said aloud

annotation.surface: A journalist is accused of helping someone who is easily taken in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reporter' looks like the journalist in the story, but here it only means someone speaking the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Succour is help given in time of need.

entries.clue: Frame that supports way over lake in part of forest (7)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue over means above, so ST comes before L
indicatorNotes.in: being in something means sitting inside it, so ST and L go inside TREE

blocks.note: a forest is made up of trees

annotation.surface: A structure carries a road over a lake in the woods.
annotation.walkthrough: The bridge picture suits a trestle, which can carry a road or railway, but the answer is built from a tree, a street and a lake.
annotation.definitionFit: A trestle is a supporting framework, like the legs under a table top.

entries.clue: It matters little I indicate after noon, provided I withdraw before the finish (14)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a sentence describing the answer: insignificance is the quality of mattering little.

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means later in the line, so SIGN is written following N
indicatorNotes.before the finish: stopping before the finish drops the last letter of CANCEL

annotation.surface: Someone shrugs that it hardly matters if they say they will pull out just before the end.
annotation.walkthrough: The two I's are used as themselves. 'It matters little' reads as a remark but describes the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the noun names the quality, and 'it matters little' is what you say of anything that has it.

entries.clue: Mineral preserved by chemicals (4)

indicatorNotes.preserved by: what is preserved by something is kept inside it, so the answer sits inside 'chemicals'

annotation.surface: A mineral sample is kept in a chemical preservative.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Preserved by' reads as pickling, but it means the answer is held within the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: Mica is a mineral that splits into thin shiny sheets.

entries.clue: Empty room hottest, a result of breaking this (10)

annotation.definition: Empty room hottest, a result of breaking this

indicatorNotes.Empty: an empty room has nothing in it, so only its outer letters R and M remain
indicatorNotes.breaking: the letters are broken up and rearranged

annotation.surface: A room gets as hot as it can once the device controlling it breaks.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a broken thermostat is exactly what leaves an empty room at its hottest.
annotation.definitionFit: A thermostat regulates temperature, so if it breaks the room can overheat.

entries.clue: Start to reel in touchy follower without restraint (6)

indicatorNotes.Start to: the start of 'reel' is its first letter, R
indicatorNotes.in: being in something means sitting inside it, so R goes inside FEELY

annotation.surface: An angler starts reeling in a sensitive fish that has been running free.
annotation.walkthrough: The follower of 'touchy' is FEELY, from the phrase touchy-feely.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to act freely is to act with nothing holding you back, which is acting without restraint.

entries.clue: Order pig to be slaughtered for food (8)

indicatorNotes.to be slaughtered: slaughtered letters are cut up and rearranged

annotation.surface: A farmer sends a pig to be killed for meat.
annotation.walkthrough: The pig suggests pork, but the food is oatmeal boiled in water or milk.
annotation.definitionFit: Porridge is a food, a breakfast of oats cooked in milk or water.
